Container.Name: EverStone
Container.Overview:
EverStone is a self-hosted, Telegram-native personal-assistant hub: the Hermes agent (Nous Research) as a Telegram gateway, plus CalDAV tasks (Radicale), Obsidian notes (CouchDB / LiveSync), and an optional browser web UI — fronted by Caddy.
This is NOT one-click. Before the first start you MUST create config.yaml in this app's appdata folder: copy config.example.yaml from the repo, fill in your Telegram bot token + owner id + passwords, and save it at the "config.yaml" host path below. (If that file does not exist, Docker creates a directory there and the container fails to start.)
After it boots, finish the one-time setup: set the model with `esadmin model <provider/model>`, and — if you use Google Calendar — run the OAuth flow. The optional web UI turns on only when you set webui.password in config.yaml.
Do NOT expose this to the internet — front it with your own HTTPS reverse proxy or Tailscale. Full deployment guide: https://github.com/mdubb86/everstone/blob/main/docs/BOOTSTRAP.md

Config.Name: Web / CalDAV / Sync port
Config.Description: Host port mapped to the container's Caddy (:80) — serves the web UI (if enabled) at /, CalDAV at /caldav, CouchDB/LiveSync at /db, and the Google OAuth callback. Point your reverse proxy / Tailscale at this port. Unraid's own UI uses 80/443, so pick a high port (e.g. 8580).

Config.Name: config.yaml (CREATE THIS FILE FIRST)
Config.Description: Your EverStone configuration and secrets. Create this file BEFORE starting: copy config.example.yaml from the repo, fill it in, and save it at this exact host path. If it does not exist, Docker will create a directory here and the container will fail. Mounted read-only.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Persistent state: CouchDB, the Obsidian vault, Radicale tasks, the Hermes profile + sessions, web-UI state, and backups. Preserve this across upgrades.
